title: Signed INT8 Multiply-Accumulate
description: Build the basic signed INT8 multiply-accumulate datapath used in DSP and machine-learning accelerators.
task: On each rising clock edge with enable high, accumulate a*b into a 32-bit signed accumulator. clear has priority over enable.
examples: a=3, b=-4, enable=1 -> acc decreases by 12
constraints: a and b are signed 8-bit values.
clear is synchronous and active high.
Hold acc when enable is low.

title: Four-Lane INT8 Dot Product
description: Implement a four-lane signed INT8 dot-product datapath similar to a small neural-network vector unit.
task: Compute a0*b0 + a1*b1 + a2*b2 + a3*b3 combinationally and return the signed result.
constraints: Use a wide enough signed result to avoid overflow for any legal inputs.
The output must be purely combinational.

title: Eight-Lane Reduction Adder
description: Create a parallel reduction block that sums eight 16-bit lanes into one output.
task: Produce the exact unsigned sum of x0 through x7 combinationally.
constraints: The output must not overflow for the maximum possible input vector.

title: ReLU with 8-bit Saturation
description: Implement a hardware activation stage that applies ReLU and saturates positive values to unsigned 8-bit range.
task: For signed 16-bit x, output 0 when x is negative, x when 0<=x<=255, and 255 when x is greater than 255.
constraints: The design must be combinational and synthesizable.

title: Systolic Array Processing Element
description: Build a single processing element for a small systolic matrix-multiply array.
task: When enable is high, forward a_in to a_out and b_in to b_out while accumulating a_in*b_in into acc. clear resets acc synchronously but still allows forwarded outputs to update only when enable is high.
examples: enable=0 -> a_out, b_out and acc hold
constraints: a and b data are signed 8-bit values.
All state updates occur on the rising clock edge.

title: Valid-Tagged Pipelined Multiplier
description: Implement a one-cycle-latency signed multiplier with an aligned valid signal, a common accelerator pipeline building block.
task: When in_valid is sampled high, capture the signed 16x16 product. Assert out_valid exactly one cycle later with the corresponding 32-bit product. Back-to-back valid inputs must be supported.
examples: in_valid with 7*-3 -> out_valid next cycle with -21
two consecutive valid inputs -> two consecutive valid outputs
constraints: The datapath must accept one input every cycle.
